Rashi on Eruvin 73a:10:1.hebrew: למקום אחר - לחצר אחרת. אביי לא שמיע ליה ההיא מתניתא דתניא לעיל [עירובין דף עב:] "חמשה שגבו את עירובן", אי נמי שמיע ליה, ומיבעיא ליה הלכתא מאי, משום דאוקימנא לה בפלוגתא:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:10:1.english: To another place - To another courtyard. Abaye had not heard that baraita that was taught above [Eruvin 72b]: “Five who collected their eiruv...”; or alternatively, he had heard it, and he was inquiring what the halakha is, since we established it as [subject to] a dispute.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:11:1.hebrew: והא אחין - דמתניתין כגבו את עירובן דמי, דהא קתני: אם אין עמהן דיורין, אין צריכין לערב:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:11:1.english: But brothers - [The brothers] of our mishna are comparable to [people] who collected their eiruv, for behold, [the mishna] teaches: If there are no [other] residents with them, they do not need to establish an eiruv.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:11:2.hebrew: הכא במאי עסקינן דאיכא דיורין בהדייהו - ומוליכין דמתניתין — אפי' בחצר שלהן קאמר, שמערבין עם דיורין שעמהן:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:11:2.english: With what are we dealing here? Where there are residents with them - And [when] the Mishnah [says] "they take [their eiruv]," it means even within their [own] courtyard, that they make an eiruv with the residents who are with them.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:11:3.hebrew: דמגו דהני אסרי - והזקיקוהו לעירוב, הני נמי אסרי איש על אחיו. אבל שתי חצירות ופתח ביניהם, וגבו אלו עירובן לעצמן והותרה חצירן, ואלו לעצמן והותרה חצירן, או שדרין באחת מהן אב ובניו בלא דיורין אחרים, ובאו לערב זו עם זו — הואיל ואין אוסר עליהן וליכא מגו, אחד נעשה שליח לכולן. דיקא נמי דטעמא משום מגו, דקתני: ״או שאין עמהן״ כו' — הא יש עמהן, דאיכא מגו, צריכין; וטעמא דרישא משום דיורין הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:11:3.english: Since these render [it] prohibited - and have necessitated an eiruv for it, these [brothers] also render [it] prohibited, each against his brother. But [in the case of] two courtyards with a doorway between them, where these [residents] collected their eiruv for themselves and their courtyard became permitted [for carrying], and those [residents collected] for themselves and their courtyard became permitted; or where a father and his sons reside in one of them without other residents, and they came to merge this [courtyard] with that [one] — since no one renders [it] prohibited for them and there is no miggo, one [person] becomes an agent for all of them. The wording [of the mishna] is also precise that the reason is on account of miggo, as it teaches: "Or when there are no [other residents] with them..." etc.; which implies that if there are [other residents] with them — where there is a miggo — they require [an eiruv for each and every one], and the reason for the first clause [of the mishna] is on account of [other] residents.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:13:1.english: In the field - An inn in the valley.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:13:3.hebrew: בבי רב - בית המדרש, ובתוך אלפים אמה הוא:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:13:3.english: In the master's house - The study hall, and it is within two thousand cubits [of the field].

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:13:4.hebrew: מבאגא משחינן להו - אלפים לכל רוח, ולא מבי רב, דבתר פיתא אזלינן, או דילמא מקום לינה גורם:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:13:4.english: Do we measure for them from the field - Two thousand [cubits] in every direction, and not from the master's house, because we follow the bread; or perhaps the place of lodging determines [it]?

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:15:1.hebrew: בההיא אנן סהדי - הואיל והוא צריך ללכת מחר לאותה הרוח, אי הוה ליה הלילה הזה בית דירה ללון במקום עירוב, טפי הוה ניחא ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:15:1.english: In that [case] we are witnesses - Since he needs to go tomorrow in that direction, if he had a dwelling this night to lodge at the place of the *eiruv*, it would be more preferable to him.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:15:2.hebrew: ה"ג - דאי מייתי ליה ריפתא לבי רב, טפי ניחא ליה:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:15:2.english: This is the reading - That if [one] brings him bread to the master’s house, it is more preferable to him.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:16:1.hebrew: האב ובנו הרב ותלמידו כרבים דמו - לענין שתי חצירות זו לפנים מזו, ודריסת רגל הפנימית על החיצונה; ותנן במתניתין [לקמן (עירובין עה.)]: אם היו של יחידים — שיחיד דר בפנימית, דהויא רגל המותרת במקומה — אינה אוסרת שלא במקומה; ואם של רבים, ולא עירבה פנימית לעצמה — דהויא רגל האסורה במקומה — אוסרת על החיצונה, אפי' עירבה חיצונה לעצמה:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:16:1.english: A father and his son, [or] a master and his student, are they considered as many - Regarding the matter of two courtyards, one within the other, and the right of passage of the inner [courtyard] through the outer [courtyard]; and we learned in our Mishnah [below (Eruvin 75a)]: If they belonged to individuals — where an individual resides in the inner [courtyard], so that it is a foot permitted in its place — it does not prohibit outside its place; and if [it belonged to] many, and the inner [courtyard] did not make an eiruv for itself — so that it is a foot prohibited in its place — it prohibits [carrying in] the outer [courtyard], even if the outer [courtyard] made an eiruv for itself.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:16:2.english: They require an eiruv - [In a case] where there are no other residents with them.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:16:3.hebrew: ניתר בלחי וקורה - דקי"ל, אין מבוי ניתר בלחי וקורה עד שיהו בתים וחצירות פתוחים לתוכו. ואת"ל הני כיחידים דמו — הכא, מי חשבינן שתי חצירות, אחת של אב ואחת של בן, כחדא חצר, ולא מישתרי מבוי דידהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:16:3.english: Is permitted through a side post and beam - For we maintain that an alleyway is not permitted through a side post and beam unless there are houses and courtyards open into it. And if you say [that] these are considered like individuals — here, do we consider two courtyards, one of the father and one of the son, as one courtyard, and [thus] their alleyway is not permitted?

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:17:1.hebrew: ומבוי שלהן ניתר בלחי וקורה - לערב חצירות, ואע"ג דאין צריכין — מ"מ פתוחות לו:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:17:1.english: And their alleyway is permitted through a side post and a cross beam - [That they are considered like individuals applies only with respect] to establishing an eiruv for the courtyards; and even though they do not need [to do so], nevertheless [distinct courtyards] open into it.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:18:1.english: (Five courtyards open into one another) (*):(*) [They] established an eiruv in the courtyards - Also from one [courtyard] to another.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:18:2.english: And they are prohibited in the alleyway - For one does not rely on an eiruv in place of a shituf.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:1:1.english: The place of bread - Where he eats.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:2:1.english: Fig watchmen - Watchmen of figs spread out in the field to dry them into dried figs.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:2:2.hebrew: בזמן שדרכן ללין בעיר - במקום שאוכלין, אע"פ שקדש עליהן היום בשדה, יש להן מן העיר אלפים לכל רוח, וכל העיר להן כד' אמות:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:2:2.english: When they customarily sleep in the city - [That is,] in the place where they eat. Even though the day became sanctified upon them in the field, they have two thousand [cubits] from the city in each direction, and the entire city is to them like four cubits.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:2:3.hebrew: בזמן שדרכן ללין בשדה - אע"פ שאוכלין בעיר, אין מודדין להן אלא מן השדה:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:2:3.english: When they customarily sleep in the field - Even though they eat in the city, one measures for them only from the field.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:3:1.hebrew: ה"ג דאי ממטו להו ריפתא להתם טפי ניחא להו - הואיל וצריכין לשמור, שהרי ישנים שם כל הלילה:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:3:1.english: This is the correct reading: “That if they brought them bread there, it would be more convenient for them” - Since they need to guard, for they sleep there all night.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:4:1.hebrew: לא שמיע לי הא שמעתא - דאמר רב: מקום פיתא גורם. רב יוסף חלה ושכח תלמודו, והיה אביי תלמידו מזכירו:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:4:1.english: I have not heard this teaching - That Rav said: The place of bread determines [one’s residence]. Rav Yosef had fallen ill and forgotten his learning, and Abaye, his disciple, would remind him.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:5:1.english: Receive a portion - And each one has a dwelling of her own, [along] with him in the courtyard.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:5:2.english: Prohibits in the case of the slaves - For they are not drawn after him.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:7:1.hebrew: בתרע מלכא - בכ"מ שהוא, חשיב ליה בתרע מלכא:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:7:1.english: In the gate of the king - In whatever place he is, he is considered [to be] in the gate of the king.

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:8:1.hebrew: תלמיד אצל רבו - דר עמו בחצר, ומקבל פרס הימנו — מאי:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:8:1.english: A student with his master - [One who] lives with him in the courtyard and receives sustenance from him — what [is the law]?

Rashi on Eruvin 73a:9:1.hebrew: דרב בי ר' חייא - כשהיה מקבל פרס מבי ר' חייא:
Rashi on Eruvin 73a:9:1.english: As Rav in the house of Rabbi Ḥiyya - When he was receiving sustenance from the house of Rabbi Ḥiyya.

Tosafot on Eruvin 73a:10:1.hebrew: בעא מיניה אביי מרבה חמשה שגבו עירובן כו' - ואע"ג דאביי ידע להאי ברייתא דלעיל — דהא בסוף פרק מי שהוציאוהו (לעיל עירובין דף מט:) פריך מינה לרבה, דקאמר ליה: "לדידך קשה, לשמואל קשה" גבי עירוב משום קנין — לא שאל כאן לרבה אלא כדי להקשות לו ממתניתין:
Tosafot on Eruvin 73a:10:1.english: "Abaye raised a dilemma before Rabba: Five who collected their eiruv, etc." - And even though Abaye knew this baraita [cited] above — for at the end of the chapter [entitled] Mi Shehotzi'uhu (above, Eruvin 49b), he raised an objection from it to Rabba, where he said to him: "According to your [view] it is difficult, [and] according to Shmuel it is difficult," regarding [the position that] an eiruv is on account of acquisition — he asked Rabba here only in order to challenge him from the Mishnah.

Tosafot on Eruvin 73a:16:1.hebrew: כרבים דמו או כיחידים דמו - פי' בקונטרס לענין ב' חצירות זו לפנים מזו, דתנן בסוף פירקין: "ואם היו של יחידים, אין צריכין לערב". ומיבעיא ליה: אם אב ובנו דרים בפנימית, אי חשיבי כיחידים או כרבים? תימה לר"י, דממתני' שמעינן ליה, דמוכחא דאין אב ובנו אוסרים זה על זה; וכיון דלא אסרי, אם כן הויא לה רגל המותרת במקומה ואינה אוסרת שלא במקומה — דההיא טעמא דיחידים אין צריכין לערב! וי"ל: דמקבלי פרס מיבעיא ליה, ומספקא ליה: אי מתני' בסמוכין על שלחן אביהם ממש, והתם הוא דאין צריכין לערב כשאין עמהם דיורין, דאהני קצת מה שסמוכים בפת, אע"ג דמקום לינה גורם; אבל מקבלי פרס, אע"ג דאין עמהם דיורין, צריכין לערב? או דילמא מתניתין במקבלי פרס, כדאוקמא רב, דאמר התם: "מקום פיתא גורם", ומייתי ראייה מברייתא דסתם האב ובנו, הרב ותלמידו, מקבלי פרס נינהו, כיון שישנים בבתיהם, היכא דלא קתני בהדיא "אוכלין על שלחן אביהן"? ומיהו לא משמע כלל לומר כן. ונראה לר"י: דמיבעיא ליה בדליכא בכל המבוי אלא אב ובנו או הרב ותלמידו, דבתים וחצירות שלהם פתוחין למבוי, וכיון שכל המבוי שלהם, משתכחת תורת עירוב; וקמיבעיא ליה נמי: דאם תימצי לומר אין צריכין לערב, מבוי שלהם ניתר בלחי וקורה או לא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 73a:16:1.english: Are they considered as many or are they considered as individuals? - Rashi explained that this pertains to two courtyards, one inside the other, as we learned in the Mishnah at the end of our chapter (75b): "And if they belonged to individuals, they do not need to make an eiruv." And he is asking: If a father and his son live in the inner [courtyard], are they considered as individuals or as many? The Ri finds this astonishing, for from our Mishnah we learn this, as it demonstrates that a father and his son do not render [carrying] prohibited for one another; and since they do not render [carrying] prohibited [for one another], if so, it becomes a foot that is permitted in its own place and does not render [carrying] prohibited outside its place — which is the very rationale that [courtyards of] individuals do not need to make an eiruv! And one can say that his dilemma concerns recipients of an allowance, and he was uncertain: Does our Mishnah refer specifically to those who are actually supported at their father's table, and it is specifically there that they do not need to make an eiruv when there are no [other] residents with them, because their being supported with bread is somewhat effective even though the place of sleeping is determining; whereas recipients of an allowance, even though there are no [other] residents with them, need to make an eiruv? Or perhaps our Mishnah refers to recipients of an allowance, in accordance with [the interpretation] established by Rav, who says there that "the place of bread is determining," and brings proof from a baraita that ordinarily a father and his son, [or] a master and his student, are recipients of an allowance, since they sleep in their houses, where it does not explicitly teach that "they eat at their father's table"? However, it does not seem plausible at all to say so. And it appears to the Ri that his dilemma concerns [a case] where there is no one in the entire alleyway except a father and his son, or a master and his student, whose houses and courtyards open into the alleyway, and since the entire alleyway belongs to them, the concept of eiruv will be forgotten; and he also asks: If you should say they do not need to make an eiruv, is their alleyway rendered permitted through a side post and beam, or not?

Tosafot on Eruvin 73a:7:1.hebrew: ודניאל בתרע מלכא - פי' ר"ח: וסימנך: בבא — שער, תרע — שער. פי': רבי יהודה בן בבא הוא מתיר בעבדים, ובבא ותרע הכל שער. נראה דמייתי קרא לסימן ולטעם לדבריו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 73a:7:1.english: “And Daniel was in the gate of the king” - Rabbeinu Chananel explained: And your mnemonic is: bava [means] gate, [and] tara [means] gate. Meaning: Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava is the one who permits in [the case of] slaves, and bava and tara are both [words for] “gate.” It appears that [Rav] cites the verse [both] as a mnemonic and as a rationale for his statement.
